title: From Brussels to Dublin: Delivering the European Open Source Strategy
content:
On 13 October, OpenForum Europe hosted the Irish edition of its Capital Series at the Smock Alley Theatre, in the heart of Dublin. As Ireland holds the Presidency of the Council of the European Union until the end of the year, the event brought Brussels-level discussions to Dublin and gave the Irish open source community the chance to engage directly with EU and national policymakers.

With the Tech Sovereignty Package published in June this year and Ireland preparing for the next phases of the AI Act implementation, our leading questions for the day were: how does the EU open source agenda translate for smaller member states and how can territories leverage open technologies and open source AI to their benefit?

Opening the day with the first keynote address, Dimitri Lorenzani, Head of Unit for Strategy and Funding Coordination for Research and Deployment Investments, DG CNECT, European Commission, said that although Europe has leading researchers and a large consumer base, 80% of its critical technologies come from outside the EU.
